# Recreation Prompt

Create a portrait-first browser-native endless runner named **Void Hustle Runner**. Preserve the source loop: a fixed-position runner, auto-scrolling platforms, one-thumb tap/double-jump, gravity, landing on safe platforms, red hazards/falls causing game over, score increasing when safe platforms pass, and instant restart. Reinterpret the world as a satirical cyber-Y2K void boulevard: the player is Sigma Drifter, a neon hover-sneaker courier outrunning boredom and parody wanted-level heat. Use procedural Canvas/CSS visuals: synthwave grid, starfield, meme billboards, cyan/magenta/lime glowing data pads, red heat traps, particle sparks, and a readable mobile HUD with REP and HEAT. Use catalog-approved sci-fi fonts and lightweight gesture-safe audio.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved source (`index_old.html`) is a canvas endless runner. The player auto-runs in place while platforms scroll left. The core objective is to survive as long as possible by tapping to jump and tapping again in the air for a double jump. Normal platforms allow landing and increase score after being passed. Red kill platforms and falling below the viewport trigger game over. Restart immediately reinitializes the same loop.

## Protected mechanics
- One-thumb tap/click plus keyboard jump input.
- Two-jump cap before landing.
- Gravity, jump impulse, side-scrolling platform movement, and platform spawning cadence.
- Axis-aligned landing and hazard collision semantics.
- Score increments only when normal platforms pass the player.
- Fail state and instant restart loop.

## Remixed target
`Void Hustle Runner` reframes the same mechanic truth as a satirical cyber-Y2K void runner. The player is Sigma Drifter, a neon hover-sneaker courier running from boredom, fake city heat, and glitch enforcement lanes. The objective remains distance/score survival, now expressed as REP and lanes cleared.

## Safe transform surfaces
Title, copy, HUD vocabulary, player silhouette, platform/hazard visuals, background world, particles, panel styling, fonts, audio choices, and feedback labels are aggressively transformed without changing play rules.
